summary: DeepSeek-V4 pools inherited mem_usage=0 and never finalized accounting. The fix records the exact nbytes of owned physical tensors for single-KV and indexer pools, then aggregates SWA or unified KV, C4/C128 KV, indexer, compression-state, backend-specific indexer, and online C128 MTP state storage in the top-level pool.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: both non-unified and unified fixtures failed because DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool had no accounting finalizer; raw output: reports/j-63239824c521/evidence/failing_before.txt

Five focused unit tests and eight subtests passed, including exact byte accounting for non-unified split indexer/state storage and the unified layout boundary; raw output: reports/j-63239824c521/evidence/unit_after_final.txt

A real non-unified DSV4 allocation on gfx950 reported 0.003348052502 GiB, exactly matching an independent sum of 3,594,944 allocated tensor bytes; raw output: reports/j-63239824c521/evidence/gpu_mem_usage_final.txt
Changed source, tests, and report artifacts contain no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution_evidence: One visible AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) executed actual torch GPU allocations for SWA, C4, C128, indexer, and compression-state buffers; reports/j-63239824c521/evidence/gpu_mem_usage_final.txt
remaining_limitations: DeepSeek-V4/DeepSeek-V4-Flash weights were not available, so a full server launch and HTTP metrics scrape were not performed.
The original eight-rank NVIDIA H100 configuration was not reproduced; validation used the assigned single AMD gfx950 GPU and does not claim multi-GPU or model-semantic coverage.
Unified-KV and backend-specific extra-buffer boundaries are covered deterministically by unit fixtures, but only the non-unified HIP allocation path was executed on hardware.
